However, there is insufficient data (Tier 4) to confidently assess its carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive, environmental, inhalation, oral, and organ/systemic hazards.
Q2: Chromium (III) is included on The Endocrine Disruption Exchange (TEDX) list due to scientific evidence suggesting endocrine disruption potential. The limited presence on other “Lists of Concern” for this substance may be partly due to significant data gaps identified across many of its hazard categories.
Q3: Chromium (III) is extensively characterized with over 20,000 scientific references, a simple and well-defined molecular formula ("Cr"), and classification as an element, indicating a clear understanding of its identity. Despite this high level of general study, its comprehensive hazard profile remains incomplete, with significant data deficiencies (Tier 4) in multiple hazard categories.
